title: Run command lost on the way to the drive
summary: A ready drive in remote control stays stopped although the PLC output is on: the command does not arrive.

sections.heading: PLC commanded is not drive accepted
sections.body: The PLC output, the terminal voltage at the PLC, the field wire, the drive terminal and the drive's own indication are separate steps. A command can be present at one and missing at the next.

sections.heading: Find the gap
sections.body: With the drive ready and in remote, compare the PLC output (LED and measured 24 V) with what the drive shows for its run terminal. The fault lies between the last point where the command is present and the first where it is missing. With a fieldbus the same reasoning applies to the communication status instead of a wire.

modeled: Generic VFD behavioral model: local/remote control place, ready chain (supply, no fault, run enable), run command, latched trip with acknowledge, terminal or keypad speed reference with a preset speed, ready/running/remote/fault relays
approximated: Linear acceleration ramp, immediate deceleration, simple motor current
omitted: Fieldbus control and its communication monitoring
Safe torque off and other safety functions

troubleshooting.effect: The drive never receives the run command
symptoms: PLC run output ON, drive stopped
repair: Repair the command path, then verify
troubleshooting.explanation: A command is only effective where it is received; diagnose the path, not just the program.
